dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I must apologize. I nearly mistook you for the type to leave your guests alone to fend for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hey, you own this place. What are you so nervous about? It's not a good look.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...It's nothing. I was just thinking about something inane.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: In your, uh... realm, some areas are completely empty.

choices.text: There's no need to fill everything to the brim. Empty space has a beauty of its own.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: You're right. Look at me, coming around here, criticizing your lifestyle choices.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: It's generous of you to host me in your home. The least I could do is be grateful.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: This is your home. Arrange it as you wish.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I'm just another person passing through.

choices.text: I'd place more things if I could, but I can't.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I get it. There are always going to be those things that are just beyond our ability to manage.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: With some things, they improve over time. With other things, the most you can do is to maintain the status quo.

choices.text: If there's something you want to say, just say it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You have the prerogative as the owner of this place. Let's hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...What, were you expecting me to start the conversation? That's probably not going to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's not so much that I have nothing to say... I just have nothing fun or positive to share.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's okay. I know what you're like.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You make it sound like that's some kind of achievement... I'm pretty frank with everyone nowadays.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Although that hasn't always been the case.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Do you know why I'm so fond of tea?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: When I drank tea for the first time, all I tasted was bitterness. No matter how much I tried to drink, there was no sign of any kind of sweet aftertaste.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: At that time, I was sitting awkwardly by some bladesmiths. I was ignorant about the conventions for human conversation and their ways of life.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Someone poured out a cup for me, and for lack of anything else to do, I accepted it. Ended up downing one cup, then another, and then another...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Now that I think back on it, they probably thought I genuinely liked to drink the stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And now?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...And now that I've had a taste of just about every flavor in this world, I've found that actually... bitterness is the one I like best.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Spices are just added extras to mask a bland base, and all sweetness does is make the ugly truth easier to stomach... But bitterness is the true flavor of life. Raw and unadulterated.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I don't care for dressing things up to make them more palatable. Life is about learning to handle the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Bitterness is what it is. It doesn't change because of what comes before or after it.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: There's no need to kid yourself into thinking that a bitter cup of tea will have a sweet aftertaste.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you want to do?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Why — you planning on helping me do it? Whatever it is?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: In that case, I need to give this some thought. I wanna find out exactly where that line is... and then see how far you can be persuaded to bend it...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Kidding.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Although the expression on your face was priceless, I'm not in the business to make you suffer just for my amusement.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If you really have nothing better to do, why don't you go find something for me to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do puppets need to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's not strictly necessary. Not for me, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But I've always found dinner tables to be extremely fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Everyone's got their own agenda, but they all have to pretend to be cordial and considerate.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Ah... what I wouldn't give to take you to one of the Harbingers' banquets.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hah, the extreme lengths they'll go to to get out of the missions they dislike...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's truly a pity that only the two of us are here. A party of two won't have any good drama.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'm not picky, so I'll eat whatever you make.

choices.text: Still, give me something to work with.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Why don't you make some of your personal favorites?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: So even if it gets painfully awkward during our meal, we can still at least enjoy the food.

choices.text: Got it. I'll go prepare a whole feast of desserts!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Eh? Why are you apologizing all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I was just conceding an error in my judgment.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Anyway, it's probably a good thing that you have a mean streak.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: I don't think I could stand to be around you if you were completely incorruptible.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Morning.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Good morning.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: A new day, a new life huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So, another ordinary day. Nothing wrong with that, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Thank you for trying to look out for me. Go get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm not done with today just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Many, many years ago, back when I still harbored the wish to become human, I prayed that I would one day be able to lead a normal life.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I never did fulfill that wish, but that doesn't mean I'm here pining ever harder for it to come true. Still... the fact that things didn't work out doesn't make my past self a fool for hoping in vain that they would, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I always found the forests in Inazuma too gloomy, and the ones in Snezhnaya too frigid.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: This one, though — seems warm, humid, teeming with life... Nothing to make me hate it so far.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Why are you so surprised? I have good moods every once in a while too, you know.
